title: Relief Valve
note: A quiet smash toy. One thumb. No scoreboard.
summary: A one-thumb occupancy loop, not a random pink game. Designed from bed-and-pain constraints: low cognitive load, zero fail states, warm light, a smash verb instead of a wellness lecture. Tap Crush. No timer, no combo, no homework.

title: Why Some Writing Sounds Like Talking
note: Prosodic Cognitive Simulation: four labs on silent reading as inner speech
summary: Interactive experiment by Nitish Chauhan. Flip controls across Working Memory Buffer, Prosodic Simulation, Delayed Closure, and Predictive Syntax to feel why some prose sounds spoken and some prose keeps resetting the inner ear.

title: Mental Models Reality Engine
note: Top priority interactive: intuition vs statistical reality
summary: Three visceral sims (Assumption Stacks, Compound Effect, Pareto Gravity) hosted on Labs. Library holds the Visceral Math note and a ten-model Cognitive Rewiring companion.
sourceFiles: Library Final - Mental Models Visceral Math

title: Hermes VPS Agent Stack
note: Telegram + WebUI face on a self-hosted agent middleware brain
summary: Hermes runs on the VPS as agent middleware - tool loop, memory, OpenAI-compatible API - while Telegram stays the fast path and a richer WebUI (chat.nitishchauhan.com) handles deep work. Open WebUI is the face; Hermes is the brains. Nitish Chauhan treats this as living personal infrastructure, not a demo chat bot.

title: Vault - Capture & Close the Loop
note: Export-first conversation capture; deliberately not a second brain
summary: Vault is a universal Chrome extension PRD: finish a chat, queue it, export Markdown/JSON/HTML/TXT, close the mental loop. Philosophy is capture-first - never summarize, rewrite, or decide what matters for you. Modular site extractors (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Cursor, generic fallback) plus an IndexedDB queue. AI memory features are explicitly out of V1 scope.

title: Memory Capture Extension (Phase 1)
note: Zero-friction highlight → silent Markdown download to Memory/Inbox
summary: Phase 1 MVP coded against the Cursor implementation guide: context menus for page, selection, and link; Turndown Markdown with a fixed metadata header; chrome.downloads to Memory/Inbox/YYYY/MM/DD; duplicate hash checks; Friction Counter CSV. No cloud, no prompts during capture. Lives under NitishLabs active-projects as the screwdriver before Vault's full queue UX.

title: Atlas / Bubble Chat
note: Thinking workspace: sessions, floating bubbles, compression - not another chat client
summary: Atlas is a spatial thinking workspace you can play in the browser: Session, Workspace, Objects, Messages. Dual modes, park and pin, compression, and demo replies without an API key. Open the live prototype, then skip into the desk.

title: Nitish AI Chat Capture
note: v1.1.0 source done; rebuild + Grok export reload still pending
summary: Earlier retrieval-grade chat capture extension: roles, offsets, hashes, and INDEX-first exports aimed at human memory first (agents inherit a clean handoff). Active-projects index marks rebuild pending after v1.1.0 dedupe/role fixes. Feeds the same problem space as Vault - preserve conversations without turning capture into a KM product.

title: Self-Compressing Knowledge Vault
note: Preserve questions first; distill knowledge denser over time - not a dump that only grows
summary: From the agent-stack design chats: a vault that compresses daily dumps and keeps the questions that generated insights, not just summaries of answers. Pairs with Atlas's compression pipeline and Hermes as the runtime that can run Historian / Scout style workers. Experiment framing - money as feedback signal on whether the artifact helps other people, not as the goal.
